member.name: M:Windows.Security.Cryptography.Core.CryptographicEngine.Encrypt(Windows.Security.Cryptography.Core.CryptographicKey,Windows.Storage.Streams.IBuffer,Windows.Storage.Streams.IBuffer)
member.summary: Encrypts data by using a symmetric or asymmetric algorithm.
member.param: Cryptographic key to use for encryption. This can be an asymmetric or a symmetric key. For more information, see AsymmetricKeyAlgorithmProvider and SymmetricKeyAlgorithmProvider.
Data to encrypt.

Buffer that contains the initialization vector. This can be **null** for a symmetric algorithm and should always be **null** for an asymmetric algorithm. If an initialization vector (IV) was used to encrypt the data, you must use the same IV to decrypt the data. You can use the GenerateRandom method to create an IV that contains random data. Other IVs, such as nonce-generated vectors, require custom implementation. For more information, see Cryptographic keys.
member.returns: Encrypted data.

member.name: M:Windows.Security.Cryptography.Core.CryptographicEngine.EncryptAndAuthenticate(Windows.Security.Cryptography.Core.CryptographicKey,Windows.Storage.Streams.IBuffer,Windows.Storage.Streams.IBuffer,Windows.Storage.Streams.IBuffer)
member.summary: Performs authenticated encryption.
member.param: Symmetric key to use for encryption.
Data to be encrypted and authenticated.

Nonce to be used. A nonce is a variable that has minimal chance of repeating. For example, you can use a random value that is newly generated for each use, a time stamp, a sequence number, or some combination of these. The Microsoft GCM implementation requires a 12-byte nonce. The CCM implementation requires a 7- to 13- byte nonce.
Authenticated data. This can be **Null**.
member.returns: The encrypted and authenticated data.If the method fails, authentication fails; if the method succeeds, the authentication succeeded as well.

member.name: F:Windows.Storage.Search.CommonFolderQuery.GroupByAlbumArtist
member.summary: Group files into virtual folders based on the System.Music.AlbumArtist property of each file. Each folder will contain all (and only) files with identical values for System.Music.AlbumArtist.

member.name: F:Windows.Storage.Search.CommonFolderQuery.GroupByArtist
member.summary: Group files into virtual folders based on the System.Music.Artist property of each file. Each folder will contain all (and only) files with identical values for System.Music.Artist.

member.name: F:Windows.Storage.Search.CommonFolderQuery.GroupByAuthor
member.summary: Group files into virtual folders based on the System.Author property of each file. Each folder will represent one author, and contain all files whose System.Author vector contains that author. If a file lists multiple authors, it may appear in more than one of the resulting folders.

member.name: F:Windows.Storage.Search.CommonFolderQuery.GroupByComposer
member.summary: Group files into virtual folders based on the System.Music.Composer property of each file. Each folder will represent one composer, and contain all files whose System.Music.Composer vector contains that composer. If a file lists multiple composers, it may appear in more than one of the resulting folders.

member.name: F:Windows.Storage.Search.CommonFolderQuery.GroupByGenre
member.summary: Group files into virtual folders based on the System.Music.Genre property of each file. Each folder will contain all (and only) files with identical values for System.Music.Genre.

member.name: F:Windows.Storage.Search.CommonFolderQuery.GroupByMonth
member.summary: Group files into virtual folders by month based on the System.ItemDate property of each file. Each folder will contain all (and only) files that have values for System.ItemDate within the same month.

member.name: F:Windows.Storage.Search.CommonFolderQuery.GroupByPublishedYear
member.summary: Group files into virtual folders by year based on the System.Media.Year property of each file. Each folder will contain all (and only) files that have values for System.Media.Year within the same year.

member.name: F:Windows.Storage.Search.CommonFolderQuery.GroupByRating
member.summary: Group files into virtual folders by rating (1 star, 2 stars, and so on) based on the System.Rating property of each file. Each folder will contain all (and only) files with identical values for System.Rating.

member.name: F:Windows.Storage.Search.CommonFolderQuery.GroupByTag
member.summary: Group files into virtual folders based on the System.Keywords property of each file. Each folder will represent one tag, and contain all files whose System.Keywords vector contains that tag. If a file lists multiple tags in its System.Keywords vector, it may appear in more than one of the resulting folders.

member.name: F:Windows.Storage.Search.CommonFolderQuery.GroupByType

member.name: F:Windows.Storage.Search.CommonFolderQuery.GroupByYear
member.summary: Group files into virtual folders by year based on the System.ItemDate property of each file. Each folder will contain all (and only) files that have values for System.ItemDate within the same year.

member.name: M:Windows.System.Diagnostics.TraceReporting.PlatformDiagnosticActions.TryEscalateScenario(System.Guid,Windows.System.Diagnostics.TraceReporting.PlatformDiagnosticEscalationType,System.String,System.Boolean,System.Boolean,Windows.Foundation.Collections.IMapView{System.String,System.String})
member.summary: Try to run a scenario on demand.
member.param: The scenario identifier.
The type of escalation.
The path to the location where the diagnostic data will be stored.
*True* to have the output directory timestamp reflect when the diagnostic data is written to the directory; *false* otherwise.
If the diagnostic scenario cannot be found on the device, *true* initiates an upload of the escalation scenario.

A dictionary of trigger and property pairs. The format is "$(T,P)=V where T is the trigger, P is the property, and V is the value. member.returns: *True* indicates the scenario was escalated; *false*, otherwise.

member.summary: Initializes a new work item with a WorkItemHandler delegate, allocating resources for the work item in advance, and specifies the priority of the work item relative to other work items in the thread pool.

member.name: M:Windows.System.Threading.Core.PreallocatedWorkItem.#ctor(Windows.System.Threading.WorkItemHandler,Windows.System.Threading.WorkItemPriority,Windows.System.Threading.WorkItemOptions)
member.summary: Initializes a new work item with a WorkItemHandler delegate, allocating resources for the work item in advance, and specifies the priority of the work item relative to other work items in the thread pool. Also specifies how the thread pool will allocate processor time for the work item.
member.param: Indicates the method that the preallocated work item will run.
The priority of the work item relative to other work items in the thread pool. The value of this parameter can be **Low**, **Normal**, or **High**.

If this parameter is set to **TimeSliced**, the work item runs simultaneously with other time-sliced work items, with each work item receiving a share of processor time. If this parameter is set to **None**, the work item runs when a worker thread becomes available.

member.returns: Provides access to the running IAsyncAction that was previously constructed and given the necessary resource allocation.

member.name: T:Windows.System.Threading.Core.SignalHandler

member.name: T:Windows.UI.Composition.CompositionStretch
member.summary: Specifies how content is scaled when mapped from its source to a destination space.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Composition.CompositionStretch.Fill
member.summary: Scale content such that its size is equal to the size of the destination. The aspect ratio of the content is not preserved.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Composition.CompositionStretch.None
member.summary: No Scaling. If the size of the content is greater than size of destination, the content is clipped to the bounds of the destination space.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Composition.CompositionStretch.Uniform
member.summary: Scale content such that its aspect ratio is preserved and it fits entirely within the bounds of the destination space. If the content’s aspect ratio does not match that of the destination, the content will not cover some of the area bound by the destination space. This is the default value for CompositionSurfaceBrush.Stretch.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Composition.CompositionStretch.UniformToFill
member.summary: Scale content such that its aspect ratio is preserved and it fills the entirety of the destination’s bounds. If the content’s aspect ratio does not match that of the destination, the content will be clipped to the bounds of the destination.

member.name: T:Windows.UI.Composition.CompositionStrokeCap
member.summary: Defines constants that specify the shape at the end of a line or segment.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Composition.CompositionStrokeCap.Flat
member.summary: A cap that does not extend past the last point of the line.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Composition.CompositionStrokeCap.Round
member.summary: A semicircle that has a diameter equal to the line thickness.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Composition.CompositionStrokeCap.Square
member.summary: Half of a square that has a length equal to the line thickness.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Core.CoreDispatcherPriority.High
member.summary: High priority. Delegates are invoked immediately for all synchronous requests. Asynchronous requests are queued and processed before any other request type.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Core.CoreDispatcherPriority.Idle
member.summary: Lowest priority. Use this priority for background tasks. Delegates are processed when the window's main thread is idle and there is no input pending in the queue.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Core.CoreDispatcherPriority.Low
member.summary: Low priority. Delegates are processed if there are no higher priority events pending in the queue.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Core.CoreDispatcherPriority.Normal
member.summary: Normal priority. Delegates are processed in the order they are scheduled.

member.name: T:Windows.UI.Input.GestureSettings
member.summary: Specifies the interactions that are supported by an application.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.GestureSettings.CrossSlide
member.summary: Enable support for the CrossSliding interaction when using the slide or swipe gesture through a single touch contact.This gesture can be used for selecting or rearranging objects.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.GestureSettings.DoubleTap
member.summary: Enable support for the double-tap gesture.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.GestureSettings.Drag
member.summary: Enable support for the slide or swipe gesture with a mouse or pen/stylus (single contact). The Dragging event is raised when either gesture is detected.This gesture can be used for text selection, selecting or rearranging objects, or scrolling and panning.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.GestureSettings.Hold
member.summary: Enable support for the press and hold gesture (from a single touch or pen/stylus contact). The Holding event is raised if a time threshold is crossed before the contact is lifted, an additional contact is detected, or a gesture is started.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.GestureSettings.HoldWithMouse
member.summary: Enable support for the press and hold gesture through the left button on a mouse. The Holding event is raised if a time threshold is crossed before the left button is released or a gesture is started.This gesture can be used to display a context menu.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.GestureSettings.ManipulationMultipleFingerPanning
member.summary: Enable panning and disable zoom when two or more touch contacts are detected.Prevents unintentional zoom interactions when panning with multiple fingers.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.GestureSettings.ManipulationRotate
member.summary: Enable support for the rotation gesture through pointer input. The ManipulationStarted, ManipulationUpdated, and ManipulationCompleted events are all raised during the course of this interaction.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.GestureSettings.ManipulationRotateInertia
member.summary: Enable support for rotation inertia after the rotate gesture (through pointer input) is complete. The ManipulationInertiaStarting event is raised if inertia is enabled.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.GestureSettings.ManipulationScale
member.summary: Enable support for the pinch or stretch gesture through pointer input.These gestures can be used for optical or semantic zoom and resizing an object. The ManipulationStarted, ManipulationUpdated, and ManipulationCompleted events are all raised during the course of this interaction.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.GestureSettings.ManipulationScaleInertia
member.summary: Enable support for scaling inertia after the pinch or stretch gesture (through pointer input) is complete. The ManipulationInertiaStarting event is raised if inertia is enabled.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.GestureSettings.ManipulationTranslateInertia
member.summary: Enable support for translation inertia after the slide gesture (through pointer input) is complete. The ManipulationInertiaStarting event is raised if inertia is enabled.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.GestureSettings.ManipulationTranslateRailsX
member.summary: Enable support for the slide gesture through pointer input, on the horizontal axis using rails (guides). The ManipulationStarted, ManipulationUpdated, and ManipulationCompleted events are all raised during the course of this interaction.This gesture can be used for rearranging objects.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.GestureSettings.ManipulationTranslateRailsY
member.summary: Enable support for the slide gesture through pointer input, on the vertical axis using rails (guides). The ManipulationStarted, ManipulationUpdated, and ManipulationCompleted events are all raised during the course of this interaction.This gesture can be used for rearranging objects.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.GestureSettings.ManipulationTranslateX
member.summary: Enable support for the slide gesture through pointer input, on the horizontal axis. The ManipulationStarted, ManipulationUpdated, and ManipulationCompleted events are all raised during the course of this interaction.This gesture can be used for rearranging objects.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.GestureSettings.ManipulationTranslateY
member.summary: Enable support for the slide gesture through pointer input, on the vertical axis. The ManipulationStarted, ManipulationUpdated, and ManipulationCompleted events are all raised during the course of this interaction.This gesture can be used for rearranging objects.

member.name: M:Windows.UI.Input.PointerPointProperties.GetUsageValue(System.UInt32,System.UInt32)
member.summary: Gets the Human Interface Device (HID) usage value of the raw input.
member.param: The Human Interface Device (HID) usage page of the pointer device. Usage pages specify the class of device. For example, touch digitizers (0x0D) and generic input (0x01).

Indicates a usage in a usage page.Usage ID specify a device or property in the **usagePage**. For example, for touch digitizers this includes tip switch (0x42) to indicate finger contact or tip pressure (0x30).
member.returns: The extended usage of the raw input pointer.

member.name: M:Windows.UI.Input.PointerPointProperties.HasUsage(System.UInt32,System.UInt32)

Indicates a usage in a usage page.Usage ID specify a device or property in the **usagePage**. For example, for touch digitizers this includes tip switch (0x42) to indicate finger contact or tip pressure (0x30).
member.returns: True if the input data includes usage information; otherwise false.

member.summary: Indicates that the pointer is departing in an abnormal manner, such as when the system receives invalid input for the pointer or when a device with active pointers departs abruptly. If the application receiving the input is in a position to do so, it should treat the interaction as not completed and reverse any effects of the pointer.

member.summary: Indicates that this pointer was captured by (associated with) another element and the original element has lost capture.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.Preview.Injection.InjectedInputPointerOptions.Confidence
member.summary: Indicates a suggestion from the source device about whether the pointer represents an intended or accidental interaction, which is especially relevant for touch pointers where an accidental interaction (such as with the palm of the hand) can trigger input. The presence of this flag indicates that the source device has high confidence that this input is part of an intended interaction.

member.summary: Indicates that the pointer is in contact with the digitizer surface or area. When this flag is not set, it indicates a hovering pointer.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.Preview.Injection.InjectedInputPointerOptions.InRange
member.summary: Indicates that the pointer continues to exist. When this flag is not set, it indicates the pointer has left detection range.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.Preview.Injection.InjectedInputPointerOptions.New

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.Preview.Injection.InjectedInputPointerOptions.PointerUp

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Input.Preview.Injection.InjectedInputPointerOptions.Primary

member.returns: The object that contains the XML.

member.name: P:Windows.UI.Notifications.BadgeNotification.ExpirationTime
member.summary: Gets or sets the time that Windows will remove the badge from the tile. By default, local badge notifications do not expire and push, periodic, and scheduled badge notifications expire after three days. It is a best practice to explicitly set an expiration time to avoid stale content.
member.returns: The date and time that the notification should be removed.

member.name: P:Windows.UI.StartScreen.SecondaryTile.LockScreenBadgeLogo
member.summary: Gets or sets the location of a badge logo image to represent the secondary tile on the lock screen. By supplying this image, you declare that the secondary tile is eligible to display a badge on the lock screen. If you also want the secondary tile to be eligible for the lock screen's detailed tile slot, you must also set the LockScreenDisplayBadgeAndTileText property to **True**.
member.returns: A Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) that specifies the logo image file location.

member.name: P:Windows.UI.StartScreen.SecondaryTile.LockScreenDisplayBadgeAndTileText
member.summary: Gets or sets whether the secondary tile is eligible to display both a badge and a detailed tile on the lock screen. If you set this property to **True**, you must also provide a badge image through the LockScreenBadgeLogo property. If you do not want to use the detailed tile capability, provide a badge image through the LockScreenBadgeLogo property and set LockScreenDisplayBadgeAndTileText to **False**.
member.returns: **True** if the secondary tile can have a lock screen presence; otherwise, **False**.

member.name: P:Windows.UI.StartScreen.VisualElementsRequest.AlternateVisualElements
member.summary: Gets a set of objects that provide alternate logo images, background and foreground colors, and display name. These alternates are shown to the user in the **Pin to Start** flyout.
member.returns: An array of SecondaryTileVisualElements objects, each of which provides the information for an alternate presentation of the secondary tile.

member.name: P:Windows.UI.StartScreen.VisualElementsRequest.Deadline
member.summary: Gets the approximate time at which the deferral will time-out.
member.returns: The time at which the deferral will time out.

member.name: P:Windows.UI.StartScreen.VisualElementsRequest.VisualElements
member.summary: Gets a copy of the parent secondary tile's SecondaryTileVisualElements object. The visual elements properties can be set or read through this object. When deferral is complete (or the handler returns without a deferral), the properties in this object are verified and then reflected in the **Pin to Start** flyout.
member.returns: The object through which you'll access the visual element properties.

member.name: M:Windows.UI.StartScreen.VisualElementsRequest.GetDeferral
member.summary: Retrieves a deferral object, which allows the app time to provide information and assets used in the **Pin to Start** flyout.
member.returns: The deferral object.

member.name: T:Windows.UI.StartScreen.VisualElementsRequestDeferral
member.summary: A deferral object used during the creation of the **Pin to Start** flyout. By using this object, the app can delay the display of the flyout while it gathers the information and assets that will be shown in that flyout.

member.name: M:Windows.UI.StartScreen.VisualElementsRequestDeferral.Complete
member.summary: Tells Windows that the app is ready to display the **Pin to Start** flyout. The app calls this method when it has finished setting the properties that specify what to show in that flyout.

member.name: T:Windows.UI.StartScreen.VisualElementsRequestedEventArgs

member.name: P:Windows.UI.StartScreen.VisualElementsRequestedEventArgs.Request

member.name: M:Windows.UI.Text.ITextRange.EndOf(Windows.UI.Text.TextRangeUnit,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Moves or extends the text range to the end of the nearest specified text unit. The text range is moved or extended forward in the document.
member.param: The unit by which to move the end position of the text range.

True extends the text range by moving just the end position of the range to the end of the specified *unit*. False moves both ends of the text range to the end of the specified *unit*. The default value is false.
member.returns: The number of character positions that the range was moved or extended, plus 1 if the text range collapsed to the start of the range. If the text range includes the final carriage return (CR) at the end of the story, and *extend* is false, the return value is set to –1 to indicate that the collapse occurred before the end of the range. This is because an insertion point cannot exist beyond the final CR.

member.name: M:Windows.UI.Text.ITextRange.Move(Windows.UI.Text.TextRangeUnit,System.Int32)
member.summary: Moves the insertion point forward or backward by the specified number of *units*. If the text range is nondegenerate, it is collapsed to an insertion point at the start or end position of the text range, depending on *count*, and then is moved.
member.param: The units to move the insertion point. The default value is **Character**.

The number of *units* to move the insertion point. The default value is 1. If *count* is greater than zero, the insertion point moves forward, toward the end of the story. If *count* is less than zero, the insertion point moves backward, toward the beginning of the story. If *count* is zero, the range is unchanged.
member.returns: The actual number of *units* the insertion point moves. For more information, see the Remarks section.

member.name: M:Windows.UI.Text.ITextRange.MoveEnd(Windows.UI.Text.TextRangeUnit,System.Int32)
member.summary: Moves the end position of the text range.
member.param: The unit by which to move the end position of the text range. The default value is **Character**.

The number of *unit*s to move the end position of the text range. The default value is 1. If *count* is greater than zero, the end position moves forward, toward the end of the story. If *count* is less than zero, the end position move backward, toward the beginning of the story. If *count* is zero, the end position does not move.
member.returns: The actual number of *unit*s that the end position of the text range moved.

member.name: M:Windows.UI.Text.ITextRange.MoveStart(Windows.UI.Text.TextRangeUnit,System.Int32)
member.summary: Moves the start position of a text range.

The number of *unit*s to move the start position of the text range. The default value is 1. If *count* is greater than zero, the start position of the text range moves forward, toward the end of the story. If *count* is less than zero, the start position of the text range moves backward, toward the beginning of the story. If *count* is zero, the start position doesn't move.
member.returns: The actual number of *unit*s that the start position moved. The pointer can be **NULL**.

member.name: M:Windows.UI.Text.ITextRange.SetIndex(Windows.UI.Text.TextRangeUnit,System.Int32,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Moves the text range to the specified unit of the story.
member.param: The *unit* used to move the text range.

The index of the specified *unit*. The text range is relocated to the *unit* that has this index. If *unit* is positive, the numbering of units begins at the start of the story and proceeds forward. If negative, the numbering begins at the end of the story and proceeds backward. The start of the story corresponds to *index* = 1 for all existing units, and the last *unit* in the story corresponds to *index* = – 1.

Indicates how to change the text range. True extends the text range to include the *unit* by moving only the end position of the text range. False collapses the text range to an insertion point and then moves the insertion point. The default value is false.

member.name: M:Windows.UI.Text.ITextRange.SetPoint(Windows.Foundation.Point,Windows.UI.Text.PointOptions,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Changes the text range based on the specified point.
member.param: An ordered pair of floating-point x- and y-coordinates that defines a point in a two-dimensional plane.
The alignment type of the specified *point*.

Indicates how to set the endpoints of the text range. If *extend* is 0, the text range is an insertion point located at the specified point, or at the nearest point with selectable text. If *extend* is 1, the endpoint specified by *options* is moved to the *point* and the other endpoint is left alone. The default value is 0.

member.name: M:Windows.UI.Text.ITextRange.SetRange(System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: Sets the endpoints of the text range to the specified values.
member.param: The character position for the start of the text range. This parameter must be less than *endPosition*.
The character position for the end of the text range.

member.summary: Moves the text range to the specified unit of the story.
member.param: The unit used to move the text range.

The index of the specified unit. The text range is relocated to the unit that has this index. If unit is positive, the numbering of units begins at the start of the story and proceeds forward. If negative, the numbering begins at the end of the story and proceeds backward. The start of the story corresponds to index = 1 for all existing units, and the last unit in the story corresponds to index = – 1.

Indicates how to change the text range. True extends the text range to include the unit by moving only the end position of the text range. False collapses the text range to an insertion point and then moves the insertion point. The default value is false.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Text.TextGetOptions.AllowFinalEop
member.summary: Allow retrieving the final end-of-paragraph (EOP) if it’s included in the range. This EOP exists in all rich-text controls and cannot be deleted. It does not exist in plain-text controls.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Text.TextGetOptions.FormatRtf
member.summary: Retrieve Rich Text Format (RTF) instead of plain text. Rich Text Format (RTF) is a BYTE (8-bit) format, but because ITextRange.GetText returns a string, the Rich Text Format (RTF) is returned as WCHARs (16-bit or UTF-16), not bytes, when you call ITextRange.GetText with the **FormatRtf** value. When you call ITextRange.SetText with **FormatRtf**, the method accepts an string containing either bytes or WCHARs, but other Rich Text Format (RTF) readers only understand bytes.

member.name: T:Windows.UI.Text.Core.CoreTextEditContext
member.summary: The primary object used by text input controls to communicate with the text input server.

member.name: P:Windows.UI.Text.Core.CoreTextEditContext.InputPaneDisplayPolicy
member.summary: Gets or sets a value that indicates whether the input pane should be shown automatically when focus enters your text input control. The default value is **Automatic**, indicating that the input pane will be shown automatically. A value of **Manual** indicates that your app will be responsible for showing and hiding the input pane using InputPane.TryShow and TryHide.
member.returns: One of the CoreTextInputPaneDisplayPolicy enumeration values. The default is **Automatic**.

member.name: P:Windows.UI.Text.Core.CoreTextEditContext.InputScope
member.summary: Gets or sets a value that indicates the input scope of the text input control.
member.returns: One of the CoreTextInputScope enumeration values. The default is **Default**.

member.name: P:Windows.UI.Text.Core.CoreTextEditContext.IsReadOnly
member.summary: Gets or sets a value that indicates whether the edit control is editable.
member.returns: **true** if the text input control is read-only; otherwise, **false**. The default is **false**.

member.name: P:Windows.UI.Text.Core.CoreTextEditContext.Name
member.summary: Gets or sets a descriptive name for the text input control. An application framework usually uses properties such as "name" or "id" to identify a control, so it’s recommended that you set this property accordingly on the text input server so that input processors can better preserve the input context, and provide better suggestions.
member.returns: A string containing a descriptive name for the text input control.

member.name: E:Windows.UI.Text.Core.CoreTextEditContext.CompositionCompleted
member.summary: Occurs when composition has completed.

member.name: E:Windows.UI.Text.Core.CoreTextEditContext.CompositionStarted
member.summary: Occurs when composition has started.

member.name: E:Windows.UI.Text.Core.CoreTextEditContext.FocusRemoved
member.summary: Occurs when focus was forcibly removed from a text input control. The application should handle this event to remove focus for the text input control accordingly.

member.name: E:Windows.UI.Text.Core.CoreTextEditContext.FormatUpdating
member.summary: Occurs when the text input server needs to apply a different format to a particular range of text. This usually happens during composition.

member.name: E:Windows.UI.Text.Core.CoreTextEditContext.LayoutRequested
member.summary: Occurs when the text input server needs to get the bounding box of a range of text and of the text input control itself. The application should handle this event and return the geometry information requested.

member.name: E:Windows.UI.Text.Core.CoreTextEditContext.NotifyFocusLeaveCompleted
member.summary: Occurs after focus has left the text input control.

member.name: E:Windows.UI.Text.Core.CoreTextEditContext.SelectionRequested
member.summary: Occurs when the text input server needs to get the text range representing the currently selected text in the text input control. The application should handle this event and return the range requested.

member.name: E:Windows.UI.Text.Core.CoreTextEditContext.SelectionUpdating
member.summary: Occurs when the text input server needs to modify the range of text currently selected in the text input control. This event could be the result of an input processor needing to select some text, or to move the caret. The text input control should set its selection range accordingly.

member.name: E:Windows.UI.Text.Core.CoreTextEditContext.TextRequested
member.summary: Occurs when the text input server needs to get a range of text from the text input control. The application should handle this event and return the range requested.

member.name: E:Windows.UI.Text.Core.CoreTextEditContext.TextUpdating
member.summary: Occurs when the text input server needs to modify text inside the text input control. This event could be the result of a key event— such as inserting a single character— or the result of processing done by an input processor, such as auto-correction and prediction.

member.name: M:Windows.UI.Text.Core.CoreTextEditContext.NotifyFocusEnter
member.summary: Notifies the text input server that focus has entered the text input control.

member.name: M:Windows.UI.Text.Core.CoreTextEditContext.NotifyFocusLeave
member.summary: Notifies the text input server that focus has left the text input control.

member.name: M:Windows.UI.Text.Core.CoreTextEditContext.NotifyLayoutChanged
member.summary: Notifies the text input server that the layout of text inside the text input control has changed.

member.name: M:Windows.UI.Text.Core.CoreTextEditContext.NotifySelectionChanged(Windows.UI.Text.Core.CoreTextRange)
member.summary: Notifies the text input server about any change that the text input control needs to make to the selection range. This is important in order to keep the internal state of the control and the internal state of the server synchronized.
member.param: The range of selection currently in effect.

member.name: M:Windows.UI.Text.Core.CoreTextEditContext.NotifyTextChanged(Windows.UI.Text.Core.CoreTextRange,System.Int32,Windows.UI.Text.Core.CoreTextRange)
member.summary: Notifies the text input server about any change that the text input control needs to make to the text. This is important in order to keep the internal state of the control and the internal state of the server synchronized. Since a change to the text is also likely to affect the selection range, the method takes the selection range as a parameter.
member.param: The range of text to replace, in terms of the state the text buffer is in prior to this text change.
The length of the text that should replace *modifiedRange*.
The range of selection in effect after the text change.

member.name: M:Windows.UI.ViewManagement.ProjectionManager.StartProjectingAsync(System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: Asynchronously sends a window (app view) to the projector or other secondary display.

The ID of the original window before projection.

member.param: The new ID of the window to be displayed by the projector or other secondary display.

member.name: M:Windows.UI.ViewManagement.ProjectionManager.StopProjectingAsync(System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: Asynchronously hides a window (app view) displayed by a projector or other secondary display.

The ID of the original window before projection.

member.name: M:Windows.UI.ViewManagement.ProjectionManager.SwapDisplaysForViewsAsync(System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: Asynchronously swaps the calling window (app view) with the window displayed on the projector or other secondary display. The result is that the calling window is displayed on the projector, and the formerly projected window is displayed on the device screen.
member.param: The ID of the window currently displayed by the projector.
The ID of the window to swap with the projected window.
member.returns: The asynchronous results of the operation. Use this to determine when the async call is complete.

member.summary: Text is trimmed at a pixel level, visually clipping the excess glyphs.

member.summary: Default.

member.name: T:Windows.UI.Xaml.TextWrapping
member.summary: Specifies whether text wraps when it reaches the edge of its container.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Xaml.TextWrapping.NoWrap
member.summary: No line wrapping is performed.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Xaml.TextWrapping.Wrap
member.summary: Line breaking occurs if a line of text overflows beyond the available width of its container. Line breaking occurs even if the text logic can't determine any line break opportunity. For example, if a very long word is constrained in a fixed-width container that can't scroll, it will wrap at a point that might be in the middle of a word.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Xaml.TextWrapping.WrapWholeWords
member.summary: Line-breaking occurs if the line overflows beyond the available block width. A line may overflow beyond the block width if the text logic can't determine a line break opportunity. For example, if a very long word is constrained in a fixed-width container that can't scroll, it will overflow the long word and continue the text after the long word on the next line. Not supported by all controls; see Remarks.

member.summary: Contains values that are used by the IScrollProvider pattern to indicate the direction and distance to scroll.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Xaml.Automation.ScrollAmount.LargeDecrement
member.summary: Specifies that scrolling is performed in large decrements, which is equivalent to pressing the PAGE UP key or to clicking a blank part of a scrollbar. If the distance represented by the PAGE UP key is not a relevant amount for the control, or if no scrollbar exists, the value represents an amount equal to the size of the currently visible window.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Xaml.Automation.ScrollAmount.LargeIncrement
member.summary: Specifies that scrolling is performed in large increments, which is equivalent to pressing the PAGE DOWN key or to clicking a blank part of a scrollbar. If the distance represented by the PAGE DOWN key is not a relevant amount for the control, or if no scrollbar exists, the value represents an amount equal to the size of the currently visible region.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Xaml.Automation.ScrollAmount.NoAmount
member.summary: Specifies that scrolling should not be performed.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Xaml.Automation.ScrollAmount.SmallDecrement
member.summary: Specifies that scrolling is performed in small decrements, which is equivalent to pressing an arrow key or to clicking the arrow button on a scrollbar.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Xaml.Automation.ScrollAmount.SmallIncrement
member.summary: Specifies that scrolling is performed in small increments, which is equivalent to pressing an arrow key or to clicking the arrow button on a scrollbar.

member.summary: Specifies the order in which to process a notification.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Xaml.Automation.Peers.AutomationNotificationProcessing.All
member.summary: These notifications should be presented to the user when possible. All of the notifications from this source should be delivered to the user.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Xaml.Automation.Peers.AutomationNotificationProcessing.CurrentThenMostRecent
member.summary: These notifications should be presented to the user when possible. Don’t interrupt the current notification for this one. If new notifications come in from the same source while the current notification is being presented, then keep the most recent and ignore the rest until the current processing is completed. Then use the most recent message as the current message.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Xaml.Automation.Peers.AutomationNotificationProcessing.ImportantAll
member.summary: These notifications should be presented to the user as soon as possible. All of the notifications from this source should be delivered to the user.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Xaml.Automation.Peers.AutomationNotificationProcessing.ImportantMostRecent
member.summary: These notifications should be presented to the user as soon as possible. The most recent notifications from this source should be delivered to the user because the most recent notification supersedes all of the other notifications.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Xaml.Automation.Peers.AutomationNotificationProcessing.MostRecent
member.summary: These notifications should be presented to the user when possible. Interrupt the current notification for this one.

member.name: M:Windows.UI.Xaml.Controls.ScrollViewer.ChangeView(Windows.Foundation.IReference{System.Double},Windows.Foundation.IReference{System.Double},Windows.Foundation.IReference{System.Single})
member.summary: Causes the ScrollViewer to load a new view into the viewport using the specified offsets and zoom factor.
member.param: A value between 0 and ScrollableWidth that specifies the distance the content should be scrolled horizontally.
A value between 0 and ScrollableHeight that specifies the distance the content should be scrolled vertically.
A value between MinZoomFactor and MaxZoomFactor that specifies the required target ZoomFactor.
member.returns: **true** if the view is changed; otherwise, **false**.

member.name: M:Windows.UI.Xaml.Controls.ScrollViewer.ChangeView(Windows.Foundation.IReference{System.Double},Windows.Foundation.IReference{System.Double},Windows.Foundation.IReference{System.Single},System.Boolean)
member.summary: Causes the ScrollViewer to load a new view into the viewport using the specified offsets and zoom factor, and optionally disables scrolling animation.
member.param: A value between 0 and ScrollableWidth that specifies the distance the content should be scrolled horizontally.
A value between 0 and ScrollableHeight that specifies the distance the content should be scrolled vertically.
A value between MinZoomFactor and MaxZoomFactor that specifies the required target ZoomFactor.
**true** to disable zoom/pan animations while changing the view; otherwise, **false**. The default is **false**.
member.returns: **true** if the view is changed; otherwise, **false**.

member.name: T:Windows.UI.Xaml.Controls.SnapPointsType
member.summary: Defines constants that specify how panning snap points are processed for gesture/manipulation input.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Xaml.Controls.SnapPointsType.Mandatory
member.summary: Content always stops at the snap point closest to where inertia would naturally stop along the direction of inertia.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Xaml.Controls.SnapPointsType.MandatorySingle
member.summary: Content always stops at the snap point closest to the release point along the direction of inertia.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Xaml.Controls.SnapPointsType.None
member.summary: No snapping behavior. Only the manipulation influences the final location.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Xaml.Controls.SnapPointsType.Optional
member.summary: Content stops at a snap point closest to where inertia would naturally stop along the direction of inertia, depending on how close the snap point is.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Xaml.Controls.SnapPointsType.OptionalSingle
member.summary: Content stops at the next snap point, if the motion starts far from it.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Xaml.Controls.SplitViewDisplayMode.CompactInline
member.summary: The amount of the pane defined by the CompactPaneLength property is shown side-by-side with the content and takes up space in the control layout. The remaining part of the pane pushes the content to the side when it's open and takes up space in the control layout. The pane does not close when the user taps outside of it.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Xaml.Controls.SplitViewDisplayMode.CompactOverlay
member.summary: The amount of the pane defined by the CompactPaneLength property is shown side-by-side with the content and takes up space in the control layout. The remaining part of the pane covers the content when it's open and does not take up space in the control layout. The pane closes when the user taps outside of it.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Xaml.Controls.SplitViewDisplayMode.Inline
member.summary: The pane is shown side-by-side with the content and takes up space in the control layout. The pane does not close when the user taps outside of it.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Xaml.Controls.SplitViewDisplayMode.Overlay
member.summary: The pane covers the content when it's open and does not take up space in the control layout. The pane closes when the user taps outside of it.

The directional heading of the camera in degrees, where 0 or 360 = North, 90 = East, 180 = South, and 270 = West. The default *headingInDegrees* value is 0.
The pitch of the map's camera in degrees, where 90 is looking out at the horizon (maximum) and 0 is looking straight down (minimum). The default *pitchInDegrees* value is 0.

member.name: M:Windows.UI.Xaml.Controls.Maps.MapCamera.#ctor(Windows.Devices.Geolocation.Geopoint,System.Double,System.Double,System.Double,System.Double)
member.summary: Creates a map camera, to define the view of a map based on location, heading, pitch, roll, and field of view.
member.param: The location of the camera in the map.
The directional heading of the camera in degrees, where 0 or 360 = North, 90 = East, 180 = South, and 270 = West. The default *headingInDegrees* value is 0.
The pitch of the map's camera in degrees, where 90 is looking out at the horizon (maximum) and 0 is looking straight down (minimum). The default *pitchInDegrees* value is 0.
The roll of the camera in degrees, where -90 is tilting to the left and +90 is tilting to the right. The default *rollInDegrees* value is 0.
The horizontal angle of view that appears in the camera, in degrees. The default *fieldOfViewInDegrees* value is 45.0.

member.summary: Creates a StreetsideExperience based on the specified panoramic view and camera position.
member.param: The panoramic view to appear in the StreetsideExperience.
The directional heading of the map's camera in degrees, where 0 or 360 = North, 90 = East, 180 = South, and 270 = West. The default *headingInDegrees* value is 0.
The pitch of the map's camera in degrees, where 90 is looking out at the horizon (maximum) and 0 is looking straight down (minimum). The default *pitchInDegrees* value is 90.
The horizontal angle of view that appears in the map's camera, in degrees. The default *fieldOfViewInDegrees* value is 75.

member.name: M:Windows.UI.Xaml.Input.PointerRoutedEventArgs.GetCurrentPoint(Windows.UI.Xaml.UIElement)
member.summary: Retrieves a PointerPoint object that provides basic info on the pointer associated with the event.
member.param: Any UIElement -derived object that is connected to the same object tree. To specify the object relative to the overall coordinate system, use a *relativeTo* value of **null**.
member.returns: A PointerPoint value that represents the pointer point associated with this event. If **null** was passed as *relativeTo*, the coordinates are in the frame of reference of the overall window. If a *relativeTo* value other than **null** was passed, the coordinates are relative to the object referenced by *relativeTo*.

member.name: M:Windows.UI.Xaml.Input.PointerRoutedEventArgs.GetIntermediatePoints(Windows.UI.Xaml.UIElement)
member.summary: Retrieves a collection of PointerPoint objects that represent the pointer history from the last pointer event up to and including the current pointer event. Each PointerPoint in the collection provides basic info on the pointer associated with the event.The last item in the collection is equivalent to the PointerPoint object returned by GetCurrentPoint.
member.param: Provides the context for the pointer data. Can be any UIElement -derived object that is connected to the same object tree. If **null**, location coordinates are in the context of the app.
member.returns: The collection of PointerPoint objects corresponding to the pointer history associated with the event. If *relativeTo* is **null**, location coordinates are in the context of the app. Otherwise, the coordinates are relative to the object referenced by *relativeTo*.

member.summary: Specifies how the intersecting areas of PathFigure objects contained in a Geometry are combined to form the area of the Geometry.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Xaml.Media.FillRule.EvenOdd
member.summary: Rule that determines whether a point is in the fill region by drawing a ray from that point to infinity in any direction and counting the number of path segments within the given shape that the ray crosses. If this number is odd, the point is inside; if even, the point is outside.

member.name: F:Windows.UI.Xaml.Media.FillRule.Nonzero
member.summary: Rule that determines whether a point is in the fill region of the path by drawing a ray from that point to infinity in any direction and then examining the places where a segment of the shape crosses the ray. Starting with a count of zero, add one each time a segment crosses the ray from left to right and subtract one each time a path segment crosses the ray from right to left. After counting the crossings, if the result is zero then the point is outside the path. Otherwise, it is inside.

member.summary: Provides utility methods that can be used to traverse object relationships (along child-object or parent-object axes) in the visual tree of your app.

member.name: M:Windows.UI.Xaml.Media.VisualTreeHelper.DisconnectChildrenRecursive(Windows.UI.Xaml.UIElement)
member.summary: Explicitly removes all references from a target UIElement, with the goal of cleaning up reference cycles.
member.param: The target object to disconnect children and remove references from.

member.name: M:Windows.UI.Xaml.Media.VisualTreeHelper.FindElementsInHostCoordinates(Windows.Foundation.Point,Windows.UI.Xaml.UIElement)
member.summary: Retrieves a set of objects that are located within a specified x-y coordinate point of an app UI. The set of objects represents the components of a visual tree that share that point.
member.param: The point to use as the determination point. This point is using the coordinate space of the app window, not of any specific element (and not of *subtree* if specified).

An object to search for. If the *subtree* object exists in the overall set of elements that exist at the specified *intersectingPoint* coordinates, then the return value contains only the *subtree* object and any objects that have a higher z-order than *subtree*, listed by inverse of z-order. If the *subtree* object doesn't exist at *intersectingPoint* coordinates, the return value will be empty.
member.returns: An enumerable set of UIElement objects in the visual tree composition at the specified point, listed by inverse of z-order.

member.name: M:Windows.UI.Xaml.Media.VisualTreeHelper.FindElementsInHostCoordinates(Windows.Foundation.Point,Windows.UI.Xaml.UIElement,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Retrieves a set of objects that are located within a specified x-y coordinate point of an app UI. The set of objects represents the components of a visual tree that share that point.
member.param: The point to use as the determination point. This point is using the coordinate space of the app window, not of any specific element (and not of *subtree* if specified).

An object to search for. If the *subtree* object exists in the overall set of elements that exist at the specified *intersectingPoint* coordinates, then the return value contains only the *subtree* object and any objects that have a higher z-order than *subtree*, listed by inverse of z-order. If the *subtree* object doesn't exist at *intersectingPoint* coordinates, the return value will be empty.
**true** to include all elements that intersect, including those elements considered to be invisible to hit testing. **false** to find only visible, hit-testable elements. The default is **false**.
member.returns: An enumerable set of UIElement objects that are determined to be located in the visual tree composition at the specified point, listed by inverse of z-order.

member.name: M:Windows.UI.Xaml.Media.VisualTreeHelper.FindElementsInHostCoordinates(Windows.Foundation.Rect,Windows.UI.Xaml.UIElement)
member.summary: Retrieves a set of objects that are located within a specified Rect frame of an app UI. The set of objects represents the components of a visual tree that share a rectangular area, and might include elements that overdraw.
member.param: The Rect to use as the determination area. This frame is using the coordinate space of the app window, not of any specific element (and not of *subtree* if specified).

An object to search for. If the *subtree* object exists in the overall set of elements that exist within the specified *intersectingRect*, then the return value contains only the *subtree* object and elements that are drawing on top of its space. If the *subtree* object doesn't exist within the *intersectingRect* frame, the return value will be empty.
member.returns: An enumerable set of UIElement objects that are in the visual tree composition in the specified Rect frame.

member.name: M:Windows.UI.Xaml.Media.VisualTreeHelper.FindElementsInHostCoordinates(Windows.Foundation.Rect,Windows.UI.Xaml.UIElement,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Retrieves a set of objects that are located within a specified Rect frame of an app UI. The set of objects represents the components of a visual tree that share a rectangular area, and might include elements that overdraw.
member.param: The Rect to use as the determination area. This frame is using the coordinate space of the app window, not of any specific element (and not of *subtree* if specified).

An object to search for. If the *subtree* object exists in the overall set of elements that exist within the specified *intersectingRect*, then the return value contains only the *subtree* object and elements that are drawing on top of its space. If the *subtree* object doesn't exist within the *intersectingRect* frame, the return value will be empty.
**true** to include all elements that intersect, including those elements considered to be invisible to hit testing. **false** to find only visible, hit-testable elements. The default is **false**.
member.returns: An enumerable set of UIElement objects that are determined to be located in the visual tree composition in the specified Rect frame.

member.summary: The request could not be carried out because of a conflict on the server.

member.summary: An expectation given in an **Expect** header could not be met by the server.

member.summary: The method could not be performed on the resource because the requested action depended on another action and that action failed.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.Forbidden
member.summary: The server refuses to fulfill the request.

member.summary: The requested information is located at the URI specified in the **Location** header. The default action when this status is received is to follow the **Location** header associated with the response. When the original request method was **POST**, the redirected request will use the **GET** method.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.GatewayTimeout
member.summary: An intermediate proxy server timed out while waiting for a response from another proxy or the origin server.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.Gone
member.summary: The requested resource is no longer available.

member.summary: The requested HTTP version is not supported by the server.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.IMUsed
member.summary: The server has fulfilled a **GET** request for the resource and the response is the result of one or more actions applied to the current instance.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.InsufficientStorage
member.summary: The method could not be performed on the resource because the server is unable to store the representation needed to successfully complete the request. This condition is considered to be temporary.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.InternalServerError
member.summary: A generic error has occurred on the server.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.LengthRequired
member.summary: The required **Content-Length** header is missing.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.Locked
member.summary: The source or destination resource of a method is locked. This response should contain an appropriate precondition or post-condition code.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.LoopDetected
member.summary: The server terminated an operation because it encountered an infinite loop while processing a request. This status indicates that the entire operation failed.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.MethodNotAllowed
member.summary: The HTTP method in the request is not allowed on the requested resource.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.MovedPermanently
member.summary: The requested information has been moved to the URI specified in the **Location** header. The default action when this status is received is to follow the **Location** header associated with the response.

member.summary: The requested information has multiple representations. The default action is to treat this status as a redirect and follow the contents of the **Location** header associated with this response.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.MultiStatus

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.NetworkAuthenticationRequired

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.NoContent
member.summary: The request has been successfully processed and that the response is intentionally blank.

member.name: F:Windows.Web.Http.HttpStatusCode.NonAuthoritativeInformation
member.summary: The returned meta-information is from a cached copy instead of the origin server and therefore may be incorrect.

member.summary: The client request wasn't successful.

member.summary: The requested resource does not exist on the server.

member.summary: The server does not support the requested function.
